sources: INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open source HM Land Registry dataset for freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE is only a subset of the full Index Polygons database.
INSPIRE polygons show position and indicative extent, not an exact legal boundary.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
A Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates to a registered title.
A single registered title can contain several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon of a multi-polygon title has its own INSPIRE ID.
The full extent of a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone.
Individual title plan and register are the authoritative documents for full registered-title detail.
INSPIRE excludes leasehold and other non-freehold tenures from this open subset.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can mean unregistered land or a tenure absent from INSPIRE.
INSPIRE files are partitioned by local authority.
A polygon crossing local-authority boundaries can appear in more than one local-authority file.
INSPIRE data is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
A monthly INSPIRE publication represents data from the previous month.
Published files remain available until the next monthly release.
INSPIRE geometry and attributes are reusable under the Open Government Licence subject to attribution conditions.
Reused geometry requires both HM Land Registry and Ordnance Survey attribution.
The July 2026 INSPIRE download snapshot was published on 5 July 2026.
The download service exposes GML files by local authority.
The download page describes the polygons as indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties.
The download service does not provide an API for this dataset.
HM Land Registry supplies INSPIRE polygons in Geography Markup Language.
HM Land Registry captures the data against the British National Grid.
Polygon vertices are represented by X and Y values in British National Grid coordinates.
HM Land Registry guidance identifies British National Grid as EPSG:27700.
Reprojection is not required for terminal geometry if matching is performed in the native British National Grid.
HM Land Registry warns that conversion from British National Grid to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
Reprojected map-display geometry therefore cannot silently replace native-grid terminal geometry.
GML can be converted to GeoJSON or other formats for interoperability, but conversion is a separate processing step.
Most registered titles use the general-boundaries regime.
General boundaries do not determine the precise legal boundary line.
There is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio between title-plan general boundaries and the legal boundary.
HM Land Registry title plans are interpreted in relation to Ordnance Survey mapping and registration evidence.
A general-boundary polygon must not be relabelled as a surveyed exact legal line.
A title plan supports the register and shows the general extent of registered land.
Title plans must be read together with the register.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary has been determined under section 60.
A title plan is not a standalone proof of an exact legal boundary.
A determined boundary is the HM Land Registry mechanism for recording an exact boundary line.
A determined boundary requires the exact line to have been identified from evidence.
HM Land Registry records an already-identified exact line; it does not itself resolve where the exact line lies.
The determined-boundary plan must identify start, end and turning points.
The determined-boundary plan must state a scale and show surrounding detail sufficient for map identification.
Index-map illustrative plans do not define the extent of land in an individual title.
Official title-plan notes state that the plan shows general position, not the exact boundary line.
Measurements scaled from a title plan may not match ground measurements.
The National Data Library records HM Land Registry as publisher of INSPIRE Index Polygons.
The July 2026 data.gov.uk record identifies the INSPIRE dataset as Open Government Licence.
The data.gov.uk record also states local-authority boundary duplication can occur.
The INSPIRE metadata identifies EPSG:27700 as the spatial reference system.
HM Land Registry geospatial catalogue describes index-polygon extents as indicative of title registration.
The catalogue says title plan and title register should be consulted for full details.
The catalogue records capture scales of 1:1250 urban, 1:2500 rural and 1:10000 mountain/moorland.
GDAL GML driver can read GML2 and GML3 that can be translated to the simple-feature model.
GDAL GML parsing supports explicit parser selection.
GDAL can derive a schema by scanning when an XSD is absent, but documentation calls that approach error prone.
An explicit XSD may be supplied to avoid silent schema-discovery drift.
GDAL GML CRS handling can automatically swap coordinate order depending on srsName and options.
The GML SWAP_COORDINATES option can be pinned to YES, NO or AUTO.
For terminal identity, coordinate-swap behavior must be explicit and replayed rather than inherited from AUTO.
SKIP_CORRUPTED_FEATURES defaults to NO, allowing fail-closed parsing of corrupt features.
Setting SKIP_CORRUPTED_FEATURES=YES would silently omit bad features and is unsuitable for terminal completeness.
GDAL can expose gml:id, which can participate in feature-identity provenance.
A GML file may have multiple geometry occurrences; selected geometry path must be explicit when ambiguity exists.
GDAL geometry coordinate precision metadata can cause coordinate rounding on write.
Coordinate precision changes on conversion must not alter native input geometry used for terminal matching.
A generated .gfs cache can affect subsequent schema interpretation and must be controlled in deterministic replay.
A newer GML file causes an older .gfs cache to be ignored, so file-timestamp/cache provenance matters.
ogr2ogr can apply geometry precision operations during conversion.
Source coordinate resolution can propagate to an output layer unless explicitly unset.
Geometry conversion is diagnostic unless coordinate identity is proven against native GML.
A source CRS can be explicitly assigned and a target CRS transformation separately requested.
Coordinate-epoch and coordinate-operation options are separate provenance from raw native EPSG:27700 geometry.
Public National Polygon technical specification says an index polygon geometry is a single area.
The public technical specification exposes a unique polygon identifier lifecycle concept.
The technical specification distinguishes polygon creation and update dates.
The technical specification links polygons to title numbers in the licensed full dataset.
The open INSPIRE subset has simpler attributes than the licensed National Polygon dataset.
The licensed National Polygon service is not required for this open-source preparation path and is not a permissible paid dependency here.
Local-authority duplicate copies must be deduplicated by stable INSPIRE identity and geometry digest, not counted as distinct parcel candidates.
Multiple distinct INSPIRE polygons tied to one title must remain separate until the target point identifies the relevant component.
A point falling in more than one non-identical INSPIRE polygon is an ambiguity that must fail closed rather than choose by area or file order.
An INSPIRE polygon is suitable only as an official indicative registered-freehold extent unless stronger boundary evidence is available.
The open-source boundary manifest must preserve publication month, local authority, INSPIRE ID, raw GML hash and native CRS.
Terminal geometry membership should occur in native EPSG:27700 after an independently proven point transform, avoiding display reprojection.
No numeric legal-boundary accuracy percentage can be inferred from a general-boundary title plan or INSPIRE polygon.
Only explicit determined-boundary evidence can upgrade legal-boundary semantics from general or indicative to exact-line status.
